dictionary_entry.etymology_text: From πᾰνήγῠρῐς (pănḗgŭrĭs, “festival, assembly”) + -ῐκός (-ĭkós).

Of foreign origin, perhaps connected to πάρδαλις (párdalis). Compare the lexicographically-attested Sanskrit पुण्डरीक (puṇḍarīka, “tiger”), Sogdian 𐼾𐼴𐽀𐼹𐼻𐼸 (pwrδnk), Pashto پړانګ (pṛāng), Persian پلنگ (palang), and Hittite 𒊊𒌉𒀸 (parsnaš, “leopard”). A common folk etymology derives it from πᾰν- (păn-, “all”) + θήρ (thḗr, “beast”) or θήρα (thḗra, “hunt”).
